headline: Sheinbaum picks Beijing over Madrid
body:
Mexico's president confirmed she'll attend the APEC Leaders' Summit in Shenzhen, China (Nov 18-19) — while casting doubt on the Iberoamerican Summit in Madrid that same month.

The signal is unmistakable: when forced to choose between Asia and Europe, Mexico's calendar tilts toward the Pacific. Trade diversification isn't rhetoric anymore — it's flight bookings.

Sovereignty means choosing your own meetings.

headline: EU-Mexico trade deal signing: May 22
body:
Sheinbaum and European Council President Costa confirmed the 8th EU-Mexico Summit in Mexico City on May 22. They'll sign the Modernized Global Agreement — a decade in the making.

The deal eliminates tariffs on 86% of agricultural goods immediately. US producers are already sounding alarms about losing market share in Mexico.

Washington spent years telling Mexico "diversify" was a threat. Turns out it's a strategy — and the EU just RSVP'd.

headline: Sheinbaum's steel plan: sovereignty, not submission
body:
Mexico's new steel policy will cut imports from China and South Korea — but not because Washington said so.

The goal: protect Mexican steelmakers and build domestic industrial capacity. This isn't Trump's tariff playbook. It's industrial policy with a national interest compass.

Mexico reduces Chinese steel dependency on its own terms, for its own reasons. That's the difference between sovereignty and obedience.

headline: The China-Mexico FDI paradox
body:
Chinese FDI announcements in Mexico dropped 80% in 2025 (from $3B to $588M). Nearshoring announcements fell 78% in Q1 2026.

But here's the twist: completed Chinese projects in Q1 2026 hit $4.95 billion — investments committed before the pressure campaign kicked in.

The pipeline is real. The question is whether US pressure and USMCA uncertainty will choke the next wave — or just push it underground.

Multipolar supply chains don't disappear. They adapt.
